title: Iteration X and the Masses
summary: How Iteration X uses technicians and ordinary people.

claims.text: Technicians such as mechanics and electricians learn basic principles to keep civilisation running; keeping their numbers small makes the Masses depend on technology.
Ordinary people count for little alone, but the Convention recruits the most violent of them into paramilitary groups to break up enemy power bases.
Apprentices are usually recruited around the age of twenty, young enough to shape and old enough to use at once.

title: Time-Motion Managers (first edition)
summary: The Iteration X builders obsessed with efficiency.

claims.text: Time-Motion Managers design and oversee the building of the Technocracy's machines in fully automated factories.
The mechanical clock began with Benedictine monks around 1200 to time prayers; some say it also served Time magick.
As the Technocracy rose in the 15th and 16th centuries, the Managers' mechanics drew in the makers of industrial machines, firearms and buildings.

title: Cyber-tooth Tiger
summary: An Iteration X hunting beast of flesh and machine.

claims.text: The beast is a twelve-foot great cat over half a ton in weight, with laser barrels for eyes, diamond-coated fangs and cybernetic legs with retractable claws.
Holographic camouflage hides it, and heat and motion sensors help it track prey at night; it can tell when a target is armed.

title: Watchers and Surveyors
summary: The top of the New World Order pyramid.

claims.text: Surveyors oversee the whole war, merging telescope, space station and scout ship data with Intelligence Analysts and working with the Void Engineers.

title: New World Order devices
summary: Surveillance and escape gear of the Men in Black.

claims.text: A Green Dome manar watches a whole city from a safe house; an orbital station covers an even larger area.
Men in Black travel in black Spectre Limousines, and the Gray Men have similar cars.
Schroedinger's Closet lets an agent step into a building and travel to a Horizon realm, leaving any later Paradox to strike the empty building.

title: Ivory Tower and the field
summary: The gap between New World Order theorists and the operatives who fight.

claims.text: Administrators and scholars debate Ascension safe in the Ivory Tower, while field operatives face a world full of monsters.
San Francisco is overrun with supernatural beings; the staff of its Divisidero safe house blend with the local culture rather than look like black-suited agents.

title: FACADE Engineers
summary: Progenitors who reshape bodies, and claim the old myths as their work.

claims.text: FACADE stands for Forced Adaptation and Clone Alteration Developmental Eugenicists; they adapt humans to new environments.
They claim that early Egyptian Progenitors built the animal-headed beings later taken for gods, and that Greek ones made centaurs, the Minotaur and merfolk.

title: Cephalopoid
summary: A squid or octopus joined to a human brain and face.

claims.text: Built from a large octopus or squid, a cephalopoid has human wits and a face under its mantle; it cannot speak but may write with its tentacles.
Progenitors use them as scouts and guards on marine missions.
